key_insight: SolCloudLLM combines sky imagery and time-series data in a bidirectional multimodal fusion framework, enabling better short-term solar forecasting than unimodal LLM or deep learning baselines, especially under cloudy conditions.
engineering_relevance: More accurate PV and GHI forecasts can improve dispatch, reserve scheduling, and grid operation decisions at sites where cloud-driven ramps dominate forecast error.
method: Align sky-image patches with time-series patches
Fuse both modalities bidirectionally into a unified representation
Map the fused embedding into an LLM for forecasting
evidence_signal: On the SIRTA and SKIPP'D datasets, the method achieved the best MSE across all horizons with up to 25.4% relative reduction, and it performed especially well in few-shot and cloudy-sky settings.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on site-specific image and time-series availability, so deployment may be limited where sky cameras are sparse, poorly calibrated, or conditions differ from training.
paper_title: Bidirectional Multimodal Fusion of Sky Images and Time-Series for Solar Forecasting with Large Language Models
